correctness.rationale: Invariance of a compact interior measure permits integrating the generator applied to log(x/(1-x)), -M log x-(1-M) log(1-x) and log y. Their generator images yield exactly the stated affine means, centered covariance and susceptible-contact identity. Eliminating N produces a concave quadratic in M with leading coefficient -2/zeta, hence V=(M-beta_-)(beta_+-M). A constant x under an invariant measure forces y constant on support, proving non-Dirac implies V>0. The root sum (K+2-zeta)/2<0 and physical beta+>0 imply beta-<-beta+, so M<beta+, d=beta+-M<D/2, selects the smaller root of V=d(D-d) and produces the exact gap and strict bounds. Frieswijk et al. Theorem 2 restrictions imply zeta>K+2 by algebra and ensure an interior periodic measure; no newly proved orbit existence. Independently derived all three generator formulas and quadratic curvature symbolically; numerical period checks are not required for the exact invariant-measure proof.
residual_risks: No formal Lean proof; bounded independent calculations corroborate but are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Exact waveform-independent amplification of mean infection from measured protective-behavior variance supplies a mathematically motivated invariant for the specific epidemiological flow, valid far beyond perturbative Hopf analysis. The negative covariance and strict prevalence comparison have a direct structural interpretation, and the exact amplitude-dependent bounds are independently reusable. The conclusion is about deterministic long-run means, not intervention efficacy or welfare.
residual_risks: No new theorem on existence/uniqueness/attraction of periodic orbits.

final_claim: For every invariant probability measure with compact interior support for dx=x(1-x)(2x+zeta y-K), dy=y(R(1-x)(1-y)-mu), R,zeta,mu>0 and K>2, the exact stationary moments satisfy 2M+zeta N=K, Cov(x,y)=-2Var(x)/zeta, and (1-M)(1-N)=mu/R+2Var(x)/zeta. For any non-Dirac invariant state, V=(M-beta_-)(beta_+-M)>0 where beta± solve (1-s)(1-(K-2s)/zeta)=mu/R. When zeta>K+2 and the larger-root equilibrium is physical, N-y*=(D-sqrt(D^2-4V))/zeta>0 with explicit upper and lower bounds; thus all nonconstant interior periodic orbits in Frieswijk et al. oscillatory regime have strictly higher long-run prevalence than the equilibrium.
limitations: Only compactly interior invariant measures and deterministic mean-field SIS system, not finite stochastic networks.
Strict comparison requires zeta>K+2 and physical larger-root equilibrium.
